beats.name: hook
beats.said: A jail cell gets painted pink, and it must be one very particular shade.
beats.shown: Guard rolls magenta onto a teal brick wall in a window light shaft; camera swings to a pinned chart reading P-618 Baker-Miller Pink, 1 pint red + 1 gallon white.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: A scientist mixes a precise pink, guards repaint after a bad first coat, then joke about it.
beats.shown: Paint shop mixing (red swirls to pink), hot-pink cell with a P-618 chip card, guards laughing at a steel table with cups; dissolves at 8.05 and 11.33 s.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: One odd rule: each inmate stays exactly fifteen minutes, timed by stopwatch; first up is the largest inmate.
beats.shown: Scientist at pink door C-4 with stopwatch, a prisoner walks in, guards flank the door; the huge inmate grins in the pink cell as red cracks spread over walls and floor.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Post-treatment, the skinniest guard beats the giant at arm wrestling in two seconds, and nobody knows why.
beats.shown: Door opens on a pale smiling inmate; wide sunlit hall; arm wrestle at a steel table with the scientist raising a stopwatch; camera orbits and rises.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Within a year, prisons nationwide are repainting cells pink by the truckload.
beats.shown: Camera rises through the skylight, flies over roof and patchwork farmland, then lands in a yard where a pink truck marked P-618 arrives.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: A guard forgets a prisoner overnight: calm at fifteen minutes, pacing at twenty, then wrecking the cell.
beats.shown: Day-to-night dissolve, dozing guard at a CRT monitor, zoom into the cell; ginger prisoner sits, paces, then lifts the bench in a starburst of debris; pull-out to the hall.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Scientists claimed pink drained aggression within fifteen minutes, so prisons applied it to violent inmates, but only briefly.
beats.shown: Guards and scientist stare at the wrecked cell door; dissolve to a big inmate knitting a candy-striped scarf; a stopwatch swoops in at the left.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Stay longer than that, and it backfires completely.
beats.shown: Knitter's smile sours to a scowl, punch-in, then red cracks, shock ring and dark vignette as he flexes with red eyes; stopwatch lower-left; hard stop.

hook.first_frame: Full-body cartoon guard in a navy cap raises a paint roller on a long pole against a teal brick cell wall; hard window light shaft, pink tray lower-left, caption 'They' at about 70% height.
hook.first_3s: Guard rolls a magenta stripe down the wall in the light shaft (slow push-in, ~2 s); at 2.1 s the camera swings to a pinned chart (P-618 Baker-Miller Pink, 1 pint red + 1 gallon white) that fills the frame by 3 s.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title restates the first line's premise (pink jail cell) and adds the word experiment; it hides the 15-minute rule and the twist.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Baker-Miller pink (P-618, 1 pint red to 1 gallon white) is claimed to sap aggression for about 15 minutes, then backfire; as told in the video, not verified.
story.protagonist: The scientist (brown hair, striped tie) who sets the paint recipe and the 15-minute rule; inmates are his test subjects.
story.authority_or_antagonist: Prison guards who follow his rules; the pink cell itself flips from calming to enraging.

tone.humour: Light absurd gags: delighted guards with a doll-brand quip, a skinny guard beating a huge inmate in two seconds, a giant knitting a candy-striped scarf, then an over-the-top rage burst.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Fast deadpan narration; dramatic irony in the reversal (a calming colour makes the calm man rage); a rhetorical 'wait, what' beat after the arm-wrestle.
tone.dialogue_style: No on-screen speech: characters are mute with expression swaps; the one quoted guard remark is voiced inside the narration; captions mirror the narration only.

animation.body_motion: Puppet-like pose-to-pose motion: noodle limbs swing and bend, torso and head tilt as whole shapes (roller swing f0-f42, slam, pacing); characters often hold a pose and only drift while the camera does the work.
animation.eyes_and_blinks: Eyes are swapped sprite states (dots, half-lids, closed arcs, wide rings, red glow); no blink cycle in f480-f505 or f1866-f1896.
animation.idle_motion: Minimal: scientist sways about 1-2% of frame width with small head drift (f480-f505); knitter's hands, needles and scarf move; camera creep (2-6%/s push-in) supplies most life.
animation.squash_and_stretch: None obvious: limbs keep constant length; the finale head looks larger only through the camera punch-in (f1914-f1932); scarf and yarn stretch.

generation_evidence.observation: Wall chart text (P-618, BAKER-MILLER PINK, recipe, EXACTLY!) stays crisp and identical through a push-in and a dissolve; no letter warping.
Calendar 1979 JUNE and COFFEE note stay legible; the cell inside the CRT screen matches the full-frame cell (window, bench, tally marks, drain) after the zoom-through.
Hall details (C-4 plate, hanging cable box, ceiling lamp, cyan brick wall, floor line) and the scientist's tie stripes stay identical while the camera pulls out; no swimming textures.
Debris cubes, cracks and the bar in the prisoner's hands keep consistent positions as the camera pulls out through the door; the guard enters with the same cap design.
Faces swap between a few discrete mouth and eye sprites (grin, laugh, closed arcs) with no in-betweens; the guard designs repeat exactly across shots.
Camera rises through the hall roof with consistent floor, skylight grid and roof gravel; clean perspective and no object morphing.
